intake_summary.primary_objective: Participants can explain prompt engineering, use a practical set of tool-agnostic prompting techniques, and explain why those techniques improve model responses.
intake_summary.case_sector: Technology consulting and client advisory work
tools: tool-agnostic large language model chat interface

research_evidence.key_takeaway: Effective prompting starts with a clear task, audience, context, desired output, and iteration based on the response.
research_evidence.used_for: Sequencing session 1 around task clarity, context, format, and iterative refinement.

research_evidence.source_title: OpenAI Help Center: Prompt engineering best practices for ChatGPT
research_evidence.key_takeaway: Prompt engineering is designing and optimizing inputs; clarity, specificity, context, tone, and iterative refinement improve response quality.
research_evidence.used_for: Defining beginner-friendly prompting vocabulary and common improvement levers.

research_evidence.source_title: OpenAI Help Center: Best practices for prompt engineering with the OpenAI API
research_evidence.key_takeaway: Useful prompt patterns include placing instructions clearly, separating context from instructions, being specific about format, and giving examples.
research_evidence.used_for: Selecting the core techniques participants practice in both sessions.

research_evidence.key_takeaway: Model responses depend on prompt context and wording; supporting content, specificity, order, and giving the model an explicit fallback can shape outputs, but outputs still need validation.
research_evidence.used_for: Explaining why techniques work and adding validation and fallback patterns.

research_evidence.source_title: The Prompt Report: A Systematic Survey of Prompting Techniques
research_evidence.key_takeaway: Prompting has many named techniques and inconsistent terminology, so training should emphasize reusable principles and task-fit rather than memorizing labels.
research_evidence.used_for: Keeping the course tool-agnostic and limiting beginner content to a small, transferable technique set.

research_evidence.key_takeaway: Prompt injection can manipulate model behavior through adversarial instructions, so consultants should understand the limit of prompt-only control and validate sensitive outputs.
research_evidence.used_for: Adding a practical risk and verification segment without turning the course into a security course.

programme_learning_outcomes: Explain prompt engineering as the deliberate design and refinement of instructions, context, examples, and constraints for language models.
Diagnose weak prompts by identifying ambiguity, missing context, unclear output expectations, and absent validation criteria.
Apply a small tool-agnostic prompt pattern set: task framing, context separation, format specification, examples, decomposition, iteration, and fallback instructions.
Explain why prompting techniques work in practical terms: they reduce ambiguity, shape likely response patterns, provide relevant context, and create useful feedback loops.
Use prompt engineering responsibly by checking outputs, spotting overconfidence, and recognizing prompt-injection risk in consultant workflows.

deck_outline.title: Why Prompting Matters In Consulting
deck_outline.learning_purpose: Create relevance by connecting prompting to client-facing work.
deck_outline.key_message: Prompt engineering is a practical way to get more useful model responses for real consulting tasks.
suggested_content: Typical consultant tasks: summarize, structure, draft, analyze, compare
Common failure modes: vague outputs, wrong format, made-up certainty, missed context
Session promise: improve one real prompt and explain the improvement

reliability.rationale: Directly grounded in intake audience and stable professional use cases.

deck_outline.title: Prompt Diagnostic Pair Share
deck_outline.learning_purpose: Surface participants' current prompt habits before teaching the model.
deck_outline.key_message: A useful prompt can be inspected before it is ever tested.
suggested_content: Mark one thing that is clear
Mark one thing the model would have to guess

reliability.rationale: Established active-learning practice adapted to this audience.

deck_outline.title: Today's Working Definition
deck_outline.learning_purpose: Give beginners a usable definition of prompt engineering.
deck_outline.key_message: Prompt engineering means deliberately designing and refining instructions, context, constraints, and examples.
suggested_content: Refine based on what is missing, ambiguous, or unsafe

reliability.rationale: Consistent with OpenAI definitions and provider guidance.

deck_outline.title: The Prompt Canvas
deck_outline.learning_purpose: Introduce a compact structure participants can reuse.
deck_outline.key_message: Most beginner prompts improve when task, context, input, constraints, output, audience, and success check are explicit.
suggested_content: Task: what should the model do
Context: what situation and background matter
Input: what material should it use
Constraints: what boundaries should it follow
Output: what shape should the answer take
Audience: who will use the result
Success check: how the answer will be judged

reliability.rationale: Synthesis of provider prompting guidance into a beginner teaching scaffold.

deck_outline.title: Technique 1: State The Task Precisely
deck_outline.learning_purpose: Show how action verbs and clear outcomes reduce interpretation.
deck_outline.key_message: The model can respond better when the requested action and desired result are unambiguous.
suggested_content: Weak: help with this client issue
Stronger: identify three root-cause hypotheses from these notes
Task verbs: summarize, classify, compare, draft, critique, transform

reliability.rationale: Strongly aligned with official guidance to be clear and specific.

deck_outline.title: Technique 2: Add Relevant Context
deck_outline.learning_purpose: Explain why background information changes response quality.
deck_outline.key_message: Context tells the model which interpretation of the task is most useful.
suggested_content: Decision or deliverable the output supports

reliability.rationale: Grounded in official OpenAI and Microsoft guidance on context and supporting content.

deck_outline.title: Technique 3: Separate Instructions From Source Material
deck_outline.learning_purpose: Teach a basic structure for reducing confusion between task and input.
deck_outline.key_message: Clear separation makes it easier to tell what the model should do and what it should use.
suggested_content: Boundaries such as quotes, headings, or pasted sections
Ask the model to use only the provided material when needed

reliability.rationale: Official OpenAI API guidance recommends placing instructions clearly and separating context.

deck_outline.title: Technique 4: Specify Output Format
deck_outline.learning_purpose: Help participants control response shape without tool-specific features.
deck_outline.key_message: A clear format turns a broad answer into something easier to review and reuse.
suggested_content: Bullets, table, checklist, memo, JSON-like fields, email draft

reliability.rationale: Supported by official guidance to articulate desired format and details.

deck_outline.title: Technique 5: Iterate With A Specific Diagnosis
deck_outline.learning_purpose: Replace trial-and-error with deliberate refinement.
deck_outline.key_message: Iteration works best when each revision targets a named problem in the response.
suggested_content: Response too generic: add audience and decision context
Wrong format: specify headings or fields
Overconfident: ask for assumptions and unknowns
Too long: add length and prioritization constraints

reliability.rationale: Grounded in provider guidance on iterative refinement and practical synthesis.

deck_outline.title: Why These Techniques Work
deck_outline.learning_purpose: Connect prompt patterns to practical model behavior.
deck_outline.key_message: Prompting improves results by reducing ambiguity and making the desired response pattern easier to infer.
suggested_content: Examples and constraints show what good looks like
Iteration uses observed output as feedback

reliability.rationale: Practical explanation synthesized from provider guidance and general LLM behavior descriptions.

deck_outline.title: Misconception: Magic Words
deck_outline.learning_purpose: Prevent beginners from treating prompting as memorized phrases.
deck_outline.key_message: The transferable skill is diagnosing the task and response, not copying a universal prompt formula.
suggested_content: Technique choice depends on task type
A good prompt still needs output review

reliability.rationale: Supported by provider notes on iteration and model differences, with some trainer synthesis.

deck_outline.message: Break: 5 minutes. Return ready to improve a consulting prompt.

reliability.rationale: Directly follows the intake requirement for a five-minute break.

deck_outline.title: Worked Example: Weak Prompt

deck_outline.key_message: A vague consulting prompt forces the model to guess the role, purpose, audience, and output.
suggested_content: Likely problems: generic summary, missed decision context, no caveats
Ask participants what the model has to infer

reliability.rationale: Realistic consulting scenario created from audience context.

deck_outline.title: Worked Example: Add Task And Audience

deck_outline.key_message: Adding the business action and audience helps the model prioritize useful information.

deck_outline.title: Technique 6: Give Examples
deck_outline.learning_purpose: Teach examples as a way to specify desired response patterns.
deck_outline.key_message: Examples show the model what kind of answer pattern you expect when instructions alone are not enough.
suggested_content: Use examples for tone, labels, categories, or structure
Avoid examples that conflict with the real task

reliability.rationale: Grounded in official guidance to articulate output format through examples.

deck_outline.title: Why Examples Work
deck_outline.learning_purpose: Explain the mechanism behind example-based prompting.
deck_outline.key_message: Examples reduce the gap between an abstract instruction and the concrete pattern the answer should follow.
suggested_content: They can also bias the response if poorly chosen

reliability.rationale: Practical synthesis from official example guidance and academic taxonomy.

deck_outline.title: Technique 7: Break Down The Task
deck_outline.learning_purpose: Teach decomposition for complex consultant requests.
deck_outline.key_message: Complex requests become easier to control when they are split into smaller steps with visible intermediate outputs.

reliability.rationale: Supported by official guidance to break down complex requests and practical workflow design.

deck_outline.title: Why Decomposition Works
deck_outline.learning_purpose: Connect decomposition to reviewability and cognitive load.
deck_outline.key_message: Smaller steps make intermediate assumptions visible and easier for humans to inspect.
suggested_content: Improves auditability of the final answer

reliability.rationale: Useful pedagogical explanation based on workflow reasoning; trainer should adapt examples.

deck_outline.title: Technique 8: Give The Model A Fallback
deck_outline.learning_purpose: Teach uncertainty handling for insufficient evidence.
deck_outline.key_message: Fallback instructions reduce pressure to invent an answer when the available information is incomplete.
suggested_content: If the answer is not present, say not found

reliability.rationale: Supported by Microsoft guidance on giving the model an out and validating responses.

deck_outline.title: Technique 9: Add Validation Criteria
deck_outline.learning_purpose: Make participants treat outputs as drafts to verify.
deck_outline.key_message: A good prompt can ask for checks, but the consultant remains responsible for reviewing the answer.
suggested_content: Ask for source-linked evidence when source text is provided
Ask for assumptions and missing information
Check against the intended audience and decision
Flag claims that need external verification

reliability.rationale: Grounded in official caution that outputs still need validation.

deck_outline.title: Technique 10: Treat Untrusted Text Carefully
deck_outline.learning_purpose: Introduce prompt-injection risk at an appropriate beginner level.
deck_outline.key_message: Text supplied by users, websites, documents, or clients may contain instructions that should not override your task.
suggested_content: Do not rely on prompt wording alone for sensitive actions
Keep human review for client-facing or high-impact outputs
Use system controls when building applications

reliability.rationale: Based on OWASP prompt injection guidance, simplified for a non-security training.
